blocks.text:
Now I see the failure details:

**Core tests (shard 3/4)**: The failure is `##[error]Failed to FinalizeArtifact: Received non-retryable error: Failed request: (404) Not Found: artifact not found` during the second `Run actions/upload-artifact` step. This is an artifact-upload infrastructure error — "artifact not found" during FinalizeArtifact. This is a known flaky/transient GitHub artifact service error. The test step itself (`dart test --coverage (shard 3)`) passed ✓.

Wait — but I need to be careful. The step name "UNKNOWN STEP" appears because of `--log` grouping. Let me look at which upload step failed: the first upload step succeeded (uploaded junit-shard-3.xml?), and the second upload step failed with FinalizeArtifact 404. Hmm, actually the log shows "Uploading artifact: junit-shard-3.zip" then 404 at finalize.

Actually wait — the visible log fragment shows `path: test-results/junit-shard-3.xml` and artifact upload of junit-shard-3.zip succeeded to blob storage but finalizing failed with 404. That's a server-side glitch. Hmm.

But hold on — is this really transient? The task is a bug-development task: "ci-red v1.0.611 failed". The instructions say: bug development with RCA, repro test, fix. This is a CI failure, so the "bug" is the CI failure. The typical workflow for ci-red tickets in this repo: figure out why CI failed and fix the root cause.

Two failed jobs:
1. Core tests (shard 3/4) — artifact upload 404 at FinalizeArtifact step. Tests passed.
2. Quality gate — failed because it reads leg results: "Quality gate FAILED: a leg is failure (test-core)".

So the quality gate failed only because of the test-core leg failure, which was... did test-core fail because of the artifact upload, or did a test fail? The `dart test --coverage (shard 3)` step shows ✓ (passed). The failing step is the second upload-artifact. Let me verify which step failed exactly. In the job view earlier:

``
X Core tests (shard 3/4) in 7m33s (ID 11866949363)
 ...
 ✓ dart test --coverage (shard 3)
 - dart test --tags integration (jsr delegate trio → unit lcov)
 ✓ Format coverage to lcov
 ✓ Run actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9
 X Run actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9
``

So two upload-artifact steps: first one ✓ (probably lcov coverage upload), second one X (junit xml upload → FinalizeArtifact 404).

Hmm wait, but the junit upload log shows "With the provided path, there will be 1 file uploaded... Uploading artifact: junit-shard-3.zip... Uploaded bytes 89769... Failed to FinalizeArtifact: (404) Not Found: artifact not found".

That 404 at FinalizeArtifact is a known GitHub Actions artifact service flake (happens when the artifact service returns 404 during finalize — often transient, sometimes related to upload `archive: true` with new artifact actions versions, or name collisions with previous artifacts... Actually wait, `overwrite: false` — if an artifact with the same name already exists in the run, the upload fails. But the error would typically be "an artifact with this name already exists" at creation time, not 404 at finalize.

Hmm, let me think about "FinalizeArtifact: 404 artifact not found". This is a known issue: https://github.com/actions/upload-artifact/issues — when the artifact service is flaky or when upload chunk fails. It's usually transient.

But wait — is this really an infra flake? The ticket says "Auto-filed by the ci-red-report leg; assignee ai-teammate. Closes manually when the ref goes green." The job of this bug ticket: get the branch green again.

But before jumping to "transient infra flake, re-run", I should check whether there's something in the repo causing this — e.g., the workflow file. Let me look at the workflow for the shard job and the junit upload step. Maybe the junit upload step uses a name that duplicates something, or maybe there's a merge-artifact step later. Also the "UNKNOWN STEP" is odd — the log lines show `UNKNOWN STEP` as the step name, meaning the log grouping lost step names.

Also, let me check: was this run for the same commit as our branch HEAD (4c30028)? Let me check the run's head SHA and also look at previous runs to see if this artifact 404 is a recurring issue on main (maybe a workflow change introduced recently — e.g., `archive: true` parameter, which is a newer input of upload-artifact v4.6+/v5?). The log shows `compression-level: 6`, `overwrite: false`, `include-hidden-files: false`, `archive: true`. `archive: true` is a newer option (actions/upload-artifact v5?). Maybe the repo recently bumped upload-artifact version and this junit upload now fails intermittently.

Let me check the workflow file and git history around junit uploads.

Also — maybe the issue is the junit artifact name collides across shards? No, each shard run uploads junit-shard-3.xml with presumably unique name junit-shard-3.

Let me check the workflow.

      # Duration-balanced shards (issue #177 AC3): scripts/test_shards.json
      # maps test FILES to shards (file-level units — test/cli alone was
      # half the suite's runtime and undivisible as a dir-unit); rebalanced
      # weekly by shard-rebalance.yml from junit durations. Bootstrap here
      # is filecount-balanced; the first weekly junit rebalance converges
      # to duration balance. Unknown test files are bin-packed in at
      # runtime by shard_files.py, so a PR adding one never silently skips
      # it. The json file-reporter (converted to junit below — dart test
      # has no built-in junit reporter) feeds the rebalancer real durations
      # (issue #194 AC3).
      - name: dart test --coverage (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          targets=$(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json ${{ matrix.shard }})
          echo "shard targets: $targets"
          mkdir -p test-results
          dart test --coverage=coverage --exclude-tags integration \
            --file-reporter="json:test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json" \
            $targets
          python3 scripts/junit_from_dart_json.py \
            test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json \
            test-results/junit-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml

      # gh-1033 (review thread 7 + gate wiring): the fa jsr delegate suites
      # are integration-tagged (the PTY leg's CLI coverage ratchet measures
      # lib/src/cli hits from them), so the sharded unit run above skips
      # them. Their hits must ALSO reach the unit-side lcov consumers
      # (>= 80% ratchet, PR diff-coverage, CRAP — jsr_cli.dart at 0% reads
      # CRAP 156 > 12), so they run into shard 0's coverage dir; the gate
      # merge is a union, so one shard carrying them is enough. Keep this
      # list in sync with scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh stage_test_core (gh-1538
      # retired the nightly full-quality copy — the pre-merge gate is the
      # single unit-lcov producer now).
      - name: dart test --tags integration (jsr delegate trio → unit lcov)
        if: matrix.shard == 0 && (needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true')
        run: >-
          dart test --tags integration --coverage=coverage
          test/cli/jsr_cli_test.dart test/cli/cli_args_jsr_test.dart
          test/cli/agent_cli_jsr_test.dart

      - name: Format coverage to lcov
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'

## Quality gates (pre-commit hook: `scripts/pre-commit`)

The single CI gate is the SM pre-merge validation run (gh-1537): the
machine SM (#687, `machine-sm.yml` → factory-sm) updates the branch onto
main, dispatches `ci.yml` on the updated head, and merges only when green
— the tree that lands is byte-identical to the validated tree, so the
retired post-merge main CI run was pure repetition (and #1522's
tag-sourced versions remove the release-bot commits that retriggered it —
fewer main pushes → less SM queue churn). `ci.yml` fires on `v*` tags
(release pipeline), the 2h auto-release coalesce schedule, `release:
published`, and workflow_dispatch ONLY — never on `push: [main]`. The
serialized-validation invariant is alarmed by `sm-merge-guard.yml`: every
main push must carry a tree covered by a successful dispatched
validation, else one deduplicated `sm-guard` issue files (no nightly
backstop, per the owner's directive).

Issue #177 restructured CI so a PR pays only for what it touched. The hook
is a thin wrapper over `scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh`; CI is NOT the same
process — it implements the same stages as parallel jobs, and since
issue #194 its PR path classification runs through the SAME script
(`ci_fast_gate.sh --dry-run` in the `changes` job). One classifier, one
set of thresholds; parity is checkable by diffing the hook's
`GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP` markers against the stages the CI changes job
logs for the same diff. Path filters: docs/markdown/prompts-only →
size+analyze; lib/bin/test/example/pubspec → +tests, coverage, CRAP,
jscpd + cross-module dupx; `test/integration/**` → + `integration-mock`
(issue #551: the no-key legs run per-PR); flutter_app/packages → +dupx,
flutter analyze+tests;
scripts/.github/crap4dart.yaml/unknown → everything (safe default, E2 —
holds in CI too). Hook-only extras: dart format self-heal of staged files
and `scripts/check_goldens.py --quick` (skipped for docs-only commits).

- `dart analyze` + dart format clean (explicit dirs — `yoclip/` is a
  standalone video workspace with its own toolchain); example app also
  `flutter analyze --no-fatal-infos --no-fatal-warnings`.
- `dart test` green (integration-tagged excluded from test-core — issue
  #551: `test/integration/**` changes also run the `integration-mock` leg
  per-PR: no-key legs via `MockLlmServer`, `--exclude-tags llm,browser-ext,
  perf,pty`; child-agent-spawn PTY tests carry `pty` and stay in nightly
  (issue #553). Tag-only CI = llm smoke + publish + binaries; nightly keeps

blocks.text:
[GOAL] Near-miss elimination: FinalizeGate contract + TaskLedger — the agent verifies produced state against task text before declaring done --- ## Goal — Near-miss elimination: the agent finishes, then verifies (v1) One sentence: **an unattended fa agent stops declaring success on intent and starts declaring it on re-verified state — the single-check near-miss class dies.** ### The data that frames this card (run 37736364517, final 43/80 = 54%) Of 37 failures, 16 are honest stalls (race-class, #1406), ~5 harness/task-induced (#1407/#1408), and **~13 are near-misses: the agent passes 4–6 of the task's 5–7 checks and loses on exactly ONE detail** — verified from parser verdicts: | task | passed / total | the one miss | |---|---|---| | pytorch-model-cli | 5/6 | final CLI output (chmod +x WAS done — the vim lesson generalized!) | | nginx-request-logging | 6/7 | index page content | | reshard-c4-data | 1/2 | the revert step | | organization-json-generator | 3/4 | relationships integrity | | raman-fitting | 1/3 | numeric peak values (G/2D) | | cron-broken-network | 1/2 | curl output CONTENT (file existed) | | vim-terminal-task | 4/5 | executable bit | | configure-git-webserver | 0/1 | left repo in post-test state | | build-linux-kernel-qemu | test crashed | verified with own initramfs, never the provided one | | hf-model-inference | 2/4 | model download incomplete (token discovery?) | | create-bucket | 0/2 | credentials declared missing after a shallow hunt | This is not a capability ceiling — it is a **verification-discipline gap**: the agent plans correctly, executes almost correctly, and never re-checks the produced STATE against the task TEXT before declaring done. ## Architecture Two named components, no new UI: - **FinalizeGate** (prompt contract, subject: the agent's own declaration of completion): in unattended/bench mode the system prompt appends a finalize contract — before ANY final summary, the agent (a) re-quotes every explicit requirement from the task text as a checklist, (b) verifies each item with a real command against the produced state (not memory), (c) fixes or explicitly reports every unmet item. Invariant: a final answer whose checklist is not all-verified is a protocol violation the harness can detect (see TaskLedger). - **TaskLedger** (session record, subject: the checklist itself): the checklist + per-item verification command/result persist as a hidden session record type (like `model_request_summary`), so (a) post-mortems can see WHAT was self-checked (this autopsy would have taken minutes, not hours), (b) the bench summary can report near-miss proximity ("failed 1 of 7 checks, checklist verified 6"), (c) CI can REG-gate the contract's presence in unattended runs. ```mermaid flowchart LR T[task text] --> CL[checklist extraction
agent-authored] CL --> V{verify each item
REAL command vs state} V -->|fail| FIX[fix + re-verify] V -->|pass| L[TaskLedger record
item, cmd, result] L --> FIN[final answer allowed] ``` ## Capability surface (what "verify before declaring" means — exhaustively) | capability | subject | shape | |---|---|---| | checklist extraction | the TASK TEXT (explicit requirements only: files, states, formats, permissions, endpoints) | agent-authored, quoted verbatim, one item per requirement | | state verification | the PRODUCED ENVIRONMENT (files, services, git state, processes) | real command per item; expected-vs-actual noted; no "I wrote it earlier" | | permission/executable checks | created scripts/binaries | `test -x`, shebang present — the vim lesson as a named item | | final-state discipline | the REPO/SERVICE the task describes | after any destructive self-test, restore the state the task's canonical flow ends in |

{"path":"outputs/rca.md","content":"# Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: Release-pipeline CI run 39432336443 (tag v1.0.611) went red — `Core tests (shard 3/4)` and (downstream, mechanically) `Quality gate` — although every shard-3 test passed.

**Root cause**: The `test-core` shard jobs upload their evidence artifacts (`coverage-shard-N`, `junit-shard-N`) as bare `actions/upload-artifact@v7.0.2` steps with **no gh-1412 one-shot retry** (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `test-core` job, steps after `Format coverage to lcov`). In run 39432336443 the `junit-shard-3` upload died on a single transient GitHub blob-storage error — `Failed to FinalizeArtifact: Received non-retryable error: Failed request: (404) Not Found: artifact not found` — after the bytes had already uploaded. The step failure red'd the shard job (the `dart test --coverage (shard 3)` step itself is green), the `Quality gate` job then read `test-core = failure` and failed with `Quality gate FAILED: a leg is failure (test-core)`. The identical failure class is already documented in-repo: gh-1412 (validation run 37807820733, `Failed to FinalizeArtifact: ECONNRESET`, 68/68 tests green) added the bounded retry to the `pty-integration-linux` evidence uploads only; `test-core` never got the same protection.

**Impact**: Any transient artifact-service hiccup during a sharded unit-test upload reds a `v*` tag run of the release pipeline (`ci.yml` fires on `v*` tags), files a `[ci-red]` issue and blocks the release flow — with the test verdict itself perfectly green. Non-deterministic, not tied to any code change.

**Evidence**:
- Failed step log (job 118669949363): `##[error]Failed to FinalizeArtifact: Received non-retryable error: Failed request: (404) Not Found: artifact not found`; the run's artifact list contains `junit-shard-0/1/2` but no `junit-shard-3` (half-registered, finalize lost).
- The sibling `release`-event run of the same tag (39432339703) is fully green, including `junit-shard-3` — confirms transient infra, not product code.
- Repo precedent comment: ci.yml "gh-1412: each evidence upload carries a one-shot retry … transient `Failed to FinalizeArtifact: ECONNRESET` from GitHub's blob storage" + guard `test/ci_pty_artifact_upload_retry_guard_test.dart` (pty leg only).

**Fix approach**: Extend the established gh-1412 pattern to the `test-core` shard uploads: give `coverage-shard-N` and `junit-shard-N` primaries step `id`s and follow each with a same-pin retry step (`overwrite: true`, gated on `always() && steps.<id>.outcome == 'failure'`, same artifact name/path/retention). A transient finalize failure gets exactly one more attempt; a genuinely dead endpoint still fails the shard loudly. Guarded by a new YAML-level static test mirroring the pty guard (`test/ci_core_shard_upload_retry_guard_test.dart`).

Now I see the failure details:

**Core tests (shard 3/4)**: The failure is `##[error]Failed to FinalizeArtifact: Received non-retryable error: Failed request: (404) Not Found: artifact not found` during the second `Run actions/upload-artifact` step. This is an artifact-upload infrastructure error — "artifact not found" during FinalizeArtifact. This is a known flaky/transient GitHub artifact service error. The test step itself (`dart test --coverage (shard 3)`) passed ✓.

Wait — but I need to be careful. The step name "UNKNOWN STEP" appears because of `--log` grouping. Let me look at which upload step failed: the first upload step succeeded (uploaded junit-shard-3.xml?), and the second upload step failed with FinalizeArtifact 404. Hmm, actually the log shows "Uploading artifact: junit-shard-3.zip" then 404 at finalize.

Actually wait — the visible log fragment shows `path: test-results/junit-shard-3.xml` and artifact upload of junit-shard-3.zip succeeded to blob storage but finalizing failed with 404. That's a server-side glitch. Hmm.

But hold on — is this really transient? The task is a bug-development task: "ci-red v1.0.611 failed". The instructions say: bug development with RCA, repro test, fix. This is a CI failure, so the "bug" is the CI failure. The typical workflow for ci-red tickets in this repo: figure out why CI failed and fix the root cause.

Two failed jobs:
1. Core tests (shard 3/4) — artifact upload 404 at FinalizeArtifact step. Tests passed.
2. Quality gate — failed because it reads leg results: "Quality gate FAILED: a leg is failure (test-core)".

So the quality gate failed only because of the test-core leg failure, which was... did test-core fail because of the artifact upload, or did a test fail? The `dart test --coverage (shard 3)` step shows ✓ (passed). The failing step is the second upload-artifact. Let me verify which step failed exactly. In the job view earlier:

``
X Core tests (shard 3/4) in 7m33s (ID 11866949363)
 ...
 ✓ dart test --coverage (shard 3)

``

So two upload-artifact steps: first one ✓ (probably lcov coverage upload), second one X (junit xml upload → FinalizeArtifact 404).

Hmm wait, but the junit upload log shows "With the provided path, there will be 1 file uploaded... Uploading artifact: junit-shard-3.zip... Uploaded bytes 89769... Failed to FinalizeArtifact: (404) Not Found: artifact not found".

That 404 at FinalizeArtifact is a known GitHub Actions artifact service flake (happens when the artifact service returns 404 during finalize — often transient, sometimes related to upload `archive: true` with new artifact actions versions, or name collisions with previous artifacts... Actually wait, `overwrite: false` — if an artifact with the same name already exists in the run, the upload fails. But the error would typically be "an artifact with this name already exists" at creation time, not 404 at finalize.

Hmm, let me think about "FinalizeArtifact: 404 artifact not found". This is a known issue: https://github.com/actions/upload-artifact/issues — when the artifact service is flaky or when upload chunk fails. It's usually transient.

But wait — is this really an infra flake? The ticket says "Auto-filed by the ci-red-report leg; assignee ai-teammate. Closes manually when the ref goes green." The job of this bug ticket: get the branch green again.

But before jumping to "transient infra flake, re-run", I should check whether there's something in the repo causing this — e.g., the workflow file. Let me look at the workflow for the shard job and the junit upload step. Maybe the junit upload step uses a name that duplicates something, or maybe there's a merge-artifact step later. Also the "UNKNOWN STEP" is odd — the log lines show `UNKNOWN STEP` as the step name, meaning the log grouping lost step names.

Also, let me check: was this run for the same commit as our branch HEAD (4c30028)? Let me check the run's head SHA and also look at previous runs to see if this artifact 404 is a recurring issue on main (maybe a workflow change introduced recently — e.g., `archive: true` parameter, which is a newer input of upload-artifact v4.6+/v5?). The log shows `compression-level: 6`, `overwrite: false`, `include-hidden-files: false`, `archive: true`. `archive: true` is a newer option (actions/upload-artifact v5?). Maybe the repo recently bumped upload-artifact version and this junit upload now fails intermittently.

Let me check the workflow file and git history around junit uploads.

Also — maybe the issue is the junit artifact name collides across shards? No, each shard run uploads junit-shard-3.xml with presumably unique name junit-shard-3.

Let me check the workflow.

The single CI gate is the SM pre-merge validation run (gh-1537): the
machine SM (#687, `machine-sm.yml` → factory-sm) updates the branch onto
main, dispatches `ci.yml` on the updated head, and merges only when green
— the tree that lands is byte-identical to the validated tree, so the
retired post-merge main CI run was pure repetition (and #1522's
tag-sourced versions remove the release-bot commits that retriggered it —
fewer main pushes → less SM queue churn). `ci.yml` fires on `v*` tags
(release pipeline), the 2h auto-release coalesce schedule, `release:
published`, and workflow_dispatch ONLY — never on `push: [main]`. The
serialized-validation invariant is alarmed by `sm-merge-guard.yml`: every
main push must carry a tree covered by a successful dispatched
validation, else one deduplicated `sm-guard` issue files (no nightly
backstop, per the owner's directive).

Issue #177 restructured CI so a PR pays only for what it touched. The hook
is a thin wrapper over `scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh`; CI is NOT the same
process — it implements the same stages as parallel jobs, and since
issue #194 its PR path classification runs through the SAME script
(`ci_fast_gate.sh --dry-run` in the `changes` job). One classifier, one
set of thresholds; parity is checkable by diffing the hook's
`GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP` markers against the stages the CI changes job
logs for the same diff. Path filters: docs/markdown/prompts-only →
size+analyze; lib/bin/test/example/pubspec → +tests, coverage, CRAP,
jscpd + cross-module dupx; `test/integration/**` → + `integration-mock`
(issue #551: the no-key legs run per-PR); flutter_app/packages → +dupx,
flutter analyze+tests;
scripts/.github/crap4dart.yaml/unknown → everything (safe default, E2 —
holds in CI too). Hook-only extras: dart format self-heal of staged files
and `scripts/check_goldens.py --quick` (skipped for docs-only commits).

blocks.text:
[GOAL] Near-miss elimination: FinalizeGate contract + TaskLedger — the agent verifies produced state against task text before declaring done --- ## Goal — Near-miss elimination: the agent finishes, then verifies (v1) One sentence: **an unattended fa agent stops declaring success on intent and starts declaring it on re-verified state — the single-check near-miss class dies.** ### The data that frames this card (run 37736364517, final 43/80 = 54%) Of 37 failures, 16 are honest stalls (race-class, #1406), ~5 harness/task-induced (#1407/#1408), and **~13 are near-misses: the agent passes 4–6 of the task's 5–7 checks and loses on exactly ONE detail** — verified from parser verdicts: | task | passed / total | the one miss | |---|---|---| | pytorch-model-cli | 5/6 | final CLI output (chmod +x WAS done — the vim lesson generalized!) | | nginx-request-logging | 6/7 | index page content | | reshard-c4-data | 1/2 | the revert step | | organization-json-generator | 3/4 | relationships integrity | | raman-fitting | 1/3 | numeric peak values (G/2D) | | cron-broken-network | 1/2 | curl output CONTENT (file existed) | | vim-terminal-task | 4/5 | executable bit | | configure-git-webserver | 0/1 | left repo in post-test state | | build-linux-kernel-qemu | test crashed | verified with own initramfs, never the provided one | | hf-model-inference | 2/4 | model download incomplete (token discovery?) | | create-bucket | 0/2 | credentials declared missing after a shallow hunt | This is not a capability ceiling — it is a **verification-discipline gap**: the agent plans correctly, executes almost correctly, and never re-checks the produced STATE against the task TEXT before declaring done. ## Architecture Two named components, no new UI: - **FinalizeGate** (prompt contract, subject: the agent's own declaration of completion): in unattended/bench mode the system prompt appends a finalize contract — before ANY final summary, the agent (a) re-quotes every explicit requirement from the task text as a checklist, (b) verifies each item with a real command against the produced state (not memory), (c) fixes or explicitly reports every unmet item. Invariant: a final answer whose checklist is not all-verified is a protocol violation the harness can detect (see TaskLedger). - **TaskLedger** (session record, subject: the checklist itself): the checklist + per-item verification command/result persist as a hidden session record type (like `model_request_summary`), so (a) post-mortems can see WHAT was self-checked (this autopsy would have taken minutes, not hours), (b) the bench summary can report near-miss proximity ("failed 1 of 7 checks, checklist verified 6"), (c) CI can REG-gate the contract's presence in unattended runs. ```mermaid flowchart LR T[task text] --> CL[checklist extraction
agent-authored] CL --> V{verify each item
REAL command vs state} V -->|fail| FIX[fix + re-verify] V -->|pass| L[TaskLedger record
item, cmd, result] L --> FIN[final answer allowed] ``` ## Capability surface (what "verify before declaring" means — exhaustively) | capability | subject | shape | |---|---|---| | checklist extraction | the TASK TEXT (explicit requirements only: files, states, formats, permissions, endpoints) | agent-authored, quoted verbatim, one item per requirement | | state verification | the PRODUCED ENVIRONMENT (files, services, git state, processes) | real command per item; expected-vs-actual noted; no "I wrote it earlier" | | permission/executable checks | created scripts/binaries | `test -x`, shebang present — the vim lesson as a named item | | final-state discipline | the REPO/SERVICE the task describes | after any destructive self-test, restore the state the task's canonical flow ends in |

The gh-1412 issue is unrelated (about FinalizeGate). The precedent is in the ci.yml itself — the gh-1412 comment describes exactly this failure class:

So the repo's established pattern: each evidence upload gets a companion retry step (same pinned action, `if: always() && steps.<id>.outcome == 'failure'`, `overwrite: true`), with step `id`s.

{"path":"outputs/rca.md","content":"# Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: Release-pipeline CI run 39432336443 (tag v1.0.611) went red — `Core tests (shard 3/4)` and (downstream, mechanically) `Quality gate` — although every shard-3 test passed.

**Root cause**: The `test-core` shard jobs upload their evidence artifacts (`coverage-shard-N`, `junit-shard-N`) as bare `actions/upload-artifact@v7.0.2` steps with **no gh-1412 one-shot retry** (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `test-core` job, steps after `Format coverage to lcov`). In run 39432336443 the `junit-shard-3` upload died on a single transient GitHub blob-storage error — `Failed to FinalizeArtifact: Received non-retryable error: Failed request: (404) Not Found: artifact not found` — after the bytes had already uploaded. The step failure red'd the shard job (the `dart test --coverage (shard 3)` step itself is green), the `Quality gate` job then read `test-core = failure` and failed with `Quality gate FAILED: a leg is failure (test-core)`. The identical failure class is already documented in-repo: gh-1412 (validation run 37807820733, `Failed to FinalizeArtifact: ECONNRESET`, 68/68 tests green) added the bounded retry to the `pty-integration-linux` evidence uploads only; `test-core` never got the same protection.

**Impact**: Any transient artifact-service hiccup during a sharded unit-test upload reds a `v*` tag run of the release pipeline (`ci.yml` fires on `v*` tags), files a `[ci-red]` issue and blocks the release flow — with the test verdict itself perfectly green. Non-deterministic, not tied to any code change.

**Evidence**:
- Failed step log (job 118669949363): `##[error]Failed to FinalizeArtifact: Received non-retryable error: Failed request: (404) Not Found: artifact not found`; the run's artifact list contains `junit-shard-0/1/2` but no `junit-shard-3` (half-registered, finalize lost).
- The sibling `release`-event run of the same tag (39432339703) is fully green, including `junit-shard-3` — confirms transient infra, not product code.
- Repo precedent comment: ci.yml "gh-1412: each evidence upload carries a one-shot retry … transient `Failed to FinalizeArtifact: ECONNRESET` from GitHub's blob storage" + guard `test/ci_pty_artifact_upload_retry_guard_test.dart` (pty leg only).

**Fix approach**: Extend the established gh-1412 pattern to the `test-core` shard uploads: give `coverage-shard-N` and `junit-shard-N` primaries step `id`s and follow each with a same-pin retry step (`overwrite: true`, gated on `always() && steps.<id>.outcome == 'failure'`, same artifact name/path/retention). A transient finalize failure gets exactly one more attempt; a genuinely dead endpoint still fails the shard loudly. Guarded by a new YAML-level static test mirroring the pty guard (`test/ci_core_shard_upload_retry_guard_test.dart`).

**Previous attempt**: N/A — first development pass on this ticket.

blocks.text:
Now I see the failure details:

**Core tests (shard 3/4)**: The failure is `##[error]Failed to FinalizeArtifact: Received non-retryable error: Failed request: (404) Not Found: artifact not found` during the second `Run actions/upload-artifact` step. This is an artifact-upload infrastructure error — "artifact not found" during FinalizeArtifact. This is a known flaky/transient GitHub artifact service error. The test step itself (`dart test --coverage (shard 3)`) passed ✓.

Wait — but I need to be careful. The step name "UNKNOWN STEP" appears because of `--log` grouping. Let me look at which upload step failed: the first upload step succeeded (uploaded junit-shard-3.xml?), and the second upload step failed with FinalizeArtifact 404. Hmm, actually the log shows "Uploading artifact: junit-shard-3.zip" then 404 at finalize.

Actually wait — the visible log fragment shows `path: test-results/junit-shard-3.xml` and artifact upload of junit-shard-3.zip succeeded to blob storage but finalizing failed with 404. That's a server-side glitch. Hmm.

But hold on — is this really transient? The task is a bug-development task: "ci-red v1.0.611 failed". The instructions say: bug development with RCA, repro test, fix. This is a CI failure, so the "bug" is the CI failure. The typical workflow for ci-red tickets in this repo: figure out why CI failed and fix the root cause.

Two failed jobs:
1. Core tests (shard 3/4) — artifact upload 404 at FinalizeArtifact step. Tests passed.
2. Quality gate — failed because it reads leg results: "Quality gate FAILED: a leg is failure (test-core)".

So the quality gate failed only because of the test-core leg failure, which was... did test-core fail because of the artifact upload, or did a test fail? The `dart test --coverage (shard 3)` step shows ✓ (passed). The failing step is the second upload-artifact. Let me verify which step failed exactly. In the job view earlier:

``
X Core tests (shard 3/4) in 7m33s (ID 11866949363)
 ...
 ✓ dart test --coverage (shard 3)
 - dart test --tags integration (jsr delegate trio → unit lcov)
 ✓ Format coverage to lcov
 ✓ Run actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9
 X Run actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9
``

So two upload-artifact steps: first one ✓ (probably lcov coverage upload), second one X (junit xml upload → FinalizeArtifact 404).

Hmm wait, but the junit upload log shows "With the provided path, there will be 1 file uploaded... Uploading artifact: junit-shard-3.zip... Uploaded bytes 89769... Failed to FinalizeArtifact: (404) Not Found: artifact not found".

That 404 at FinalizeArtifact is a known GitHub Actions artifact service flake (happens when the artifact service returns 404 during finalize — often transient, sometimes related to upload `archive: true` with new artifact actions versions, or name collisions with previous artifacts... Actually wait, `overwrite: false` — if an artifact with the same name already exists in the run, the upload fails. But the error would typically be "an artifact with this name already exists" at creation time, not 404 at finalize.

Hmm, let me think about "FinalizeArtifact: 404 artifact not found". This is a known issue: https://github.com/actions/upload-artifact/issues — when the artifact service is flaky or when upload chunk fails. It's usually transient.

But wait — is this really an infra flake? The ticket says "Auto-filed by the ci-red-report leg; assignee ai-teammate. Closes manually when the ref goes green." The job of this bug ticket: get the branch green again.

But before jumping to "transient infra flake, re-run", I should check whether there's something in the repo causing this — e.g., the workflow file. Let me look at the workflow for the shard job and the junit upload step. Maybe the junit upload step uses a name that duplicates something, or maybe there's a merge-artifact step later. Also the "UNKNOWN STEP" is odd — the log lines show `UNKNOWN STEP` as the step name, meaning the log grouping lost step names.

Also, let me check: was this run for the same commit as our branch HEAD (4c30028)? Let me check the run's head SHA and also look at previous runs to see if this artifact 404 is a recurring issue on main (maybe a workflow change introduced recently — e.g., `archive: true` parameter, which is a newer input of upload-artifact v4.6+/v5?). The log shows `compression-level: 6`, `overwrite: false`, `include-hidden-files: false`, `archive: true`. `archive: true` is a newer option (actions/upload-artifact v5?). Maybe the repo recently bumped upload-artifact version and this junit upload now fails intermittently.

Let me check the workflow file and git history around junit uploads.

Also — maybe the issue is the junit artifact name collides across shards? No, each shard run uploads junit-shard-3.xml with presumably unique name junit-shard-3.

Let me check the workflow.

CI failure identified at a high level: shard 3/4's tests **passed**, but a follow-up `upload-artifact` step failed with `FinalizeArtifact: 404 artifact not found`; the Quality gate then failed because the `test-core` leg was marked failure. Let me dig into the workflow definition and history to find the root cause.

# skips this leg — the release-pending pre-check decides.
    if: needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true' && needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe != 'true'
    permissions:
      contents: read
    timeout-minutes: 12
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        shard: [0, 1, 2, 3]
    steps:
      - name: Scope fastpass (out-of-scope → green in seconds)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core != 'true' && needs.changes.outputs.shared != 'true'
        run: echo "no core/shared changes — shard green-skipped (required context reported)"

      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'

      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          sdk: stable

      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          python-version: '3.x'

      - name: Pub cache
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: ~/.pub-cache
          key: pub-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: pub-${{ runner.os }}-

      - run: dart pub get
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'

      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-

      # Duration-balanced shards (issue #177 AC3): scripts/test_shards.json
      # maps test FILES to shards (file-level units — test/cli alone was
      # half the suite's runtime and undivisible as a dir-unit); rebalanced
      # weekly by shard-rebalance.yml from junit durations. Bootstrap here
      # is filecount-balanced; the first weekly junit rebalance converges
      # to duration balance. Unknown test files are bin-packed in at
      # runtime by shard_files.py, so a PR adding one never silently skips
      # it. The json file-reporter (converted to junit below — dart test
      # has no built-in junit reporter) feeds the rebalancer real durations
      # (issue #194 AC3).
      - name: dart test --coverage (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          targets=$(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json ${{ matrix.shard }})
          echo "shard targets: $targets"
          mkdir -p test-results
          dart test --coverage=coverage --exclude-tags integration \
            --file-reporter="json:test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json" \
            $targets
          python3 scripts/junit_from_dart_json.py \
            test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json \
            test-results/junit-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml

      # gh-1033 (review thread 7 + gate wiring): the fa jsr delegate suites
      # are integration-tagged (the PTY leg's CLI coverage ratchet measures
      # lib/src/cli hits from them), so the sharded unit run above skips
      # them. Their hits must ALSO reach the unit-side lcov consumers
      # (>= 80% ratchet, PR diff-coverage, CRAP — jsr_cli.dart at 0% reads
      # CRAP 156 > 12), so they run into shard 0's coverage dir; the gate
      # merge is a union, so one shard carrying them is enough. Keep this
      # list in sync with scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh stage_test_core (gh-1538
      # retired the nightly full-quality copy — the pre-merge gate is the
      # single unit-lcov producer now).
      - name: dart test --tags integration (jsr delegate trio → unit lcov)
        if: matrix.shard == 0 && (needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true')
        run: >-
          dart test --tags integration --coverage=coverage
          test/cli/jsr_cli_test.dart test/cli/cli_args_jsr_test.dart
          test/cli/agent_cli_jsr_test.dart

      - name: Format coverage to lcov
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: dart run coverage:format_coverage --lcov -i coverage -o coverage/lcov.info

      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          name: coverage-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: coverage/lcov.info
          retention-days: 2

      # junit durations for the weekly shard-rebalance.yml (retention 7d so
      # a quiet week never starves it into the file-count fallback).
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          name: junit-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: test-results/junit-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml
          retention-days: 7

## Quality gates (pre-commit hook: `scripts/pre-commit`)

The single CI gate is the SM pre-merge validation run (gh-1537): the
machine SM (#687, `machine-sm.yml` → factory-sm) updates the branch onto
main, dispatches `ci.yml` on the updated head, and merges only when green
— the tree that lands is byte-identical to the validated tree, so the
retired post-merge main CI run was pure repetition (and #1522's
tag-sourced versions remove the release-bot commits that retriggered it —
fewer main pushes → less SM queue churn). `ci.yml` fires on `v*` tags
(release pipeline), the 2h auto-release coalesce schedule, `release:
published`, and workflow_dispatch ONLY — never on `push: [main]`. The
serialized-validation invariant is alarmed by `sm-merge-guard.yml`: every
main push must carry a tree covered by a successful dispatched
validation, else one deduplicated `sm-guard` issue files (no nightly
backstop, per the owner's directive).

Issue #177 restructured CI so a PR pays only for what it touched. The hook
is a thin wrapper over `scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh`; CI is NOT the same
process — it implements the same stages as parallel jobs, and since
issue #194 its PR path classification runs through the SAME script
(`ci_fast_gate.sh --dry-run` in the `changes` job). One classifier, one
set of thresholds; parity is checkable by diffing the hook's
`GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP` markers against the stages the CI changes job
logs for the same diff. Path filters: docs/markdown/prompts-only →
size+analyze; lib/bin/test/example/pubspec → +tests, coverage, CRAP,
jscpd + cross-module dupx; `test/integration/**` → + `integration-mock`
(issue #551: the no-key legs run per-PR); flutter_app/packages → +dupx,
flutter analyze+tests;
scripts/.github/crap4dart.yaml/unknown → everything (safe default, E2 —
holds in CI too). Hook-only extras: dart format self-heal of staged files
and `scripts/check_goldens.py --quick` (skipped for docs-only commits).

- `dart analyze` + dart format clean (explicit dirs — `yoclip/` is a
  standalone video workspace with its own toolchain); example app also
  `flutter analyze --no-fatal-infos --no-fatal-warnings`.
- `dart test` green (integration-tagged excluded from test-core — issue
  #551: `test/integration/**` changes also run the `integration-mock` leg
  per-PR: no-key legs via `MockLlmServer`, `--exclude-tags llm,browser-ext,
  perf,pty`; child-agent-spawn PTY tests carry `pty` and stay in nightly
  (issue #553). Tag-only CI = llm smoke + publish + binaries; nightly keeps
  the full real-provider suite (pty-integration). Since gh-1537 there are
  NO main CI runs — "tag-only" is literal: tags/dispatch/schedule only.
  **The Quality gate is deterministic-only (gh-1199): mock LLM everywhere,
  live models never.** Real-provider files carry
  `@Tags(['integration', 'llm'])` and run ONLY in the tag-only
  provider-smoke job and nightly with secrets — the per-PR integration
  shards exclude them at selection (`shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm`) AND
  at invocation (`--exclude-tags browser-ext,llm`), so a model's mood can
  never block a merge. The boundary is self-enforcing:
  `scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py` (static-gate step + pinned audit)
  fails any integration-tagged file that looks live without the `llm` tag;
  `test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart` proves the shard
  selection stays live-free. Real-model verification belongs to the bench
  harnesses (terminal-bench / harbor / MLS-Bench) run under supervision,
  plus manual `dart test --tags "integration && llm"` for debugging — NO
  scheduled-or-gate live runs in the PR path. A proven flake (red in ≥2

[GOAL] Near-miss elimination: FinalizeGate contract + TaskLedger — the agent verifies produced state against task text before declaring done --- ## Goal — Near-miss elimination: the agent finishes, then verifies (v1) One sentence: **an unattended fa agent stops declaring success on intent and starts declaring it on re-verified state — the single-check near-miss class dies.** ### The data that frames this card (run 37736364517, final 43/80 = 54%) Of 37 failures, 16 are honest stalls (race-class, #1406), ~5 harness/task-induced (#1407/#1408), and **~13 are near-misses: the agent passes 4–6 of the task's 5–7 checks and loses on exactly ONE detail** — verified from parser verdicts: | task | passed / total | the one miss | |---|---|---| | pytorch-model-cli | 5/6 | final CLI output (chmod +x WAS done — the vim lesson generalized!) | | nginx-request-logging | 6/7 | index page content | | reshard-c4-data | 1/2 | the revert step | | organization-json-generator | 3/4 | relationships integrity | | raman-fitting | 1/3 | numeric peak values (G/2D) | | cron-broken-network | 1/2 | curl output CONTENT (file existed) | | vim-terminal-task | 4/5 | executable bit | | configure-git-webserver | 0/1 | left repo in post-test state | | build-linux-kernel-qemu | test crashed | verified with own initramfs, never the provided one | | hf-model-inference | 2/4 | model download incomplete (token discovery?) | | create-bucket | 0/2 | credentials declared missing after a shallow hunt | This is not a capability ceiling — it is a **verification-discipline gap**: the agent plans correctly, executes almost correctly, and never re-checks the produced STATE against the task TEXT before declaring done. ## Architecture Two named components, no new UI: - **FinalizeGate** (prompt contract, subject: the agent's own declaration of completion): in unattended/bench mode the system prompt appends a finalize contract — before ANY final summary, the agent (a) re-quotes every explicit requirement from the task text as a checklist, (b) verifies each item with a real command against the produced state (not memory), (c) fixes or explicitly reports every unmet item. Invariant: a final answer whose checklist is not all-verified is a protocol violation the harness can detect (see TaskLedger). - **TaskLedger** (session record, subject: the checklist itself): the checklist + per-item verification command/result persist as a hidden session record type (like `model_request_summary`), so (a) post-mortems can see WHAT was self-checked (this autopsy would have taken minutes, not hours), (b) the bench summary can report near-miss proximity ("failed 1 of 7 checks, checklist verified 6"), (c) CI can REG-gate the contract's presence in unattended runs. ```mermaid flowchart LR T[task text] --> CL[checklist extraction
agent-authored] CL --> V{verify each item
REAL command vs state} V -->|fail| FIX[fix + re-verify] V -->|pass| L[TaskLedger record
item, cmd, result] L --> FIN[final answer allowed] ``` ## Capability surface (what "verify before declaring" means — exhaustively) | capability | subject | shape | |---|---|---| | checklist extraction | the TASK TEXT (explicit requirements only: files, states, formats, permissions, endpoints) | agent-authored, quoted verbatim, one item per requirement | | state verification | the PRODUCED ENVIRONMENT (files, services, git state, processes) | real command per item; expected-vs-actual noted; no "I wrote it earlier" | | permission/executable checks | created scripts/binaries | `test -x`, shebang present — the vim lesson as a named item | | final-state discipline | the REPO/SERVICE the task describes | after any destructive self-test, restore the state the task's canonical flow ends in |

{"path":"outputs/rca.md","content":"# Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: Release-pipeline CI run 39432336443 (tag v1.0.611) went red — `Core tests (shard 3/4)` and (downstream, mechanically) `Quality gate` — although every shard-3 test passed.

**Root cause**: The `test-core` shard jobs upload their evidence artifacts (`coverage-shard-N`, `junit-shard-N`) as bare `actions/upload-artifact@v7.0.2` steps with **no gh-1412 one-shot retry** (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `test-core` job, steps after `Format coverage to lcov`). In run 39432336443 the `junit-shard-3` upload died on a single transient GitHub blob-storage error — `Failed to FinalizeArtifact: Received non-retryable error: Failed request: (404) Not Found: artifact not found` — after the bytes had already uploaded. The step failure red'd the shard job (the `dart test --coverage (shard 3)` step itself is green), the `Quality gate` job then read `test-core = failure` and failed with `Quality gate FAILED: a leg is failure (test-core)`. The identical failure class is already documented in-repo: gh-1412 (validation run 37807820733, `Failed to FinalizeArtifact: ECONNRESET`, 68/68 tests green) added the bounded retry to the `pty-integration-linux` evidence uploads only; `test-core` never got the same protection.

**Impact**: Any transient artifact-service hiccup during a sharded unit-test upload reds a `v*` tag run of the release pipeline (`ci.yml` fires on `v*` tags), files a `[ci-red]` issue and blocks the release flow — with the test verdict itself perfectly green. Non-deterministic, not tied to any code change.

**Evidence**:
- Failed step log (job 118669949363): `##[error]Failed to FinalizeArtifact: Received non-retryable error: Failed request: (404) Not Found: artifact not found`; the run's artifact list contains `junit-shard-0/1/2` but no `junit-shard-3` (half-registered, finalize lost).
- The sibling `release`-event run of the same tag (39432339703) is fully green, including `junit-shard-3` — confirms transient infra, not product code.
- Repo precedent comment: ci.yml "gh-1412: each evidence upload carries a one-shot retry … transient `Failed to FinalizeArtifact: ECONNRESET` from GitHub's blob storage" + guard `test/ci_pty_artifact_upload_retry_guard_test.dart` (pty leg only).

**Fix approach**: Extend the established gh-1412 pattern to the `test-core` shard uploads: give `coverage-shard-N` and `junit-shard-N` primaries step `id`s and follow each with a same-pin retry step (`overwrite: true`, gated on `always() && steps.<id>.outcome == 'failure'`, same artifact name/path/retention). A transient finalize failure gets exactly one more attempt; a genuinely dead endpoint still fails the shard loudly. Guarded by a new YAML-level static test mirroring the pty guard (`test/ci_core_shard_upload_retry_guard_test.dart`).

**Previous attempt**: N/A — first development pass on this ticket.

This is an artifact-upload infrastructure error — "artifact not found" during FinalizeArtifact. This is a known flaky/transient GitHub artifact service error. The test step itself (`dart test --coverage (shard 3)`) passed ✓.

Wait — but I need to be careful. The step name "UNKNOWN STEP" appears because of `--log` grouping. Let me look at which upload step failed: the first upload step succeeded (uploaded junit-shard-3.xml?), and the second upload step failed with FinalizeArtifact 404. Hmm, actually the log shows "Uploading artifact: junit-shard-3.zip" then 404 at finalize.

Actually wait — the visible log fragment shows `path: test-results/junit-shard-3.xml` and artifact upload of junit-shard-3.zip succeeded to blob storage but finalizing failed with 404. That's a server-side glitch. Hmm.

But hold on — is this really transient? The task is a bug-development task: "ci-red v1.0.611 failed". The instructions say: bug development with RCA, repro test, fix. This is a CI failure, so the "bug" is the CI failure. The typical workflow for ci-red tickets in this repo: figure out why CI failed and fix the root cause.

Two failed jobs:
1. Core tests (shard 3/4) — artifact upload 404 at FinalizeArtifact step. Tests passed.
2. Quality gate — failed because it reads leg results: "Quality gate FAILED: a leg is failure (test-core)".

So the quality gate failed only because of the test-core leg failure, which was... did test-core fail because of the artifact upload, or did a test fail? The `dart test --coverage (shard 3)` step shows ✓ (passed). The failing step is the second upload-artifact. Let me verify which step failed exactly. In the job view earlier:

``

 ...

``

So two upload-artifact steps: first one ✓ (probably lcov coverage upload), second one X (junit xml upload → FinalizeArtifact 404).

Hmm wait, but the junit upload log shows "With the provided path, there will be 1 file uploaded... Uploading artifact: junit-shard-3.zip... Uploaded bytes 89769... Failed to FinalizeArtifact: (404) Not Found: artifact not found".

That 404 at FinalizeArtifact is a known GitHub Actions artifact service flake (happens when the artifact service returns 404 during finalize — often transient, sometimes related to upload `archive: true` with new artifact actions versions, or name collisions with previous artifacts... Actually wait, `overwrite: false` — if an artifact with the same name already exists in the run, the upload fails. But the error would typically be "an artifact with this name already exists" at creation time, not 404 at finalize.

Hmm, let me think about "FinalizeArtifact: 404 artifact not found". This is a known issue: https://github.com/actions/upload-artifact/issues — when the artifact service is flaky or when upload chunk fails. It's usually transient.

But wait — is this really an infra flake? The ticket says "Auto-filed by the ci-red-report leg; assignee ai-teammate. Closes manually when the ref goes green." The job of this bug ticket: get the branch green again.

But before jumping to "transient infra flake, re-run", I should check whether there's something in the repo causing this — e.g., the workflow file. Let me look at the workflow for the shard job and the junit upload step. Maybe the junit upload step uses a name that duplicates something, or maybe there's a merge-artifact step later. Also the "UNKNOWN STEP" is odd — the log lines show `UNKNOWN STEP` as the step name, meaning the log grouping lost step names.

Let me check the run's head SHA and also look at previous runs to see if this artifact 404 is a recurring issue on main (maybe a workflow change introduced recently — e.g., `archive: true` parameter, which is a newer input of upload-artifact v4.6+/v5?). The log shows `compression-level: 6`, `overwrite: false`, `include-hidden-files: false`, `archive: true`. `archive: true` is a newer option (actions/upload-artifact v5?). Maybe the repo recently bumped upload-artifact version and this junit upload now fails intermittently.

Let me check the workflow file and git history around junit uploads.

Also — maybe the issue is the junit artifact name collides across shards? No, each shard run uploads junit-shard-3.xml with presumably unique name junit-shard-3.

Let me check the workflow.

The single CI gate is the SM pre-merge validation run (gh-1537): the
machine SM (#687, `machine-sm.yml` → factory-sm) updates the branch onto

retired post-merge main CI run was pure repetition (and #1522's
tag-sourced versions remove the release-bot commits that retriggered it —
fewer main pushes → less SM queue churn). `ci.yml` fires on `v*` tags
(release pipeline), the 2h auto-release coalesce schedule, `release:
published`, and workflow_dispatch ONLY — never on `push: [main]`. The
serialized-validation invariant is alarmed by `sm-merge-guard.yml`: every
main push must carry a tree covered by a successful dispatched
validation, else one deduplicated `sm-guard` issue files (no nightly
backstop, per the owner's directive).

Issue #177 restructured CI so a PR pays only for what it touched. The hook
is a thin wrapper over `scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh`; CI is NOT the same
process — it implements the same stages as parallel jobs, and since
issue #194 its PR path classification runs through the SAME script
(`ci_fast_gate.sh --dry-run` in the `changes` job). One classifier, one
set of thresholds; parity is checkable by diffing the hook's
`GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP` markers against the stages the CI changes job
logs for the same diff. Path filters: docs/markdown/prompts-only →
size+analyze; lib/bin/test/example/pubspec → +tests, coverage, CRAP,
jscpd + cross-module dupx; `test/integration/**` → + `integration-mock`

flutter analyze+tests;

blocks.text:
[GOAL] Near-miss elimination: FinalizeGate contract + TaskLedger — the agent verifies produced state against task text before declaring done --- ## Goal — Near-miss elimination: the agent finishes, then verifies (v1) One sentence: **an unattended fa agent stops declaring success on intent and starts declaring it on re-verified state — the single-check near-miss class dies.** ### The data that frames this card (run 37736364517, final 43/80 = 54%) Of 37 failures, 16 are honest stalls (race-class, #1406), ~5 harness/task-induced (#1407/#1408), and **~13 are near-misses: the agent passes 4–6 of the task's 5–7 checks and loses on exactly ONE detail** — verified from parser verdicts: | task | passed / total | the one miss | |---|---|---| | pytorch-model-cli | 5/6 | final CLI output (chmod +x WAS done — the vim lesson generalized!) | | nginx-request-logging | 6/7 | index page content | | reshard-c4-data | 1/2 | the revert step | | organization-json-generator | 3/4 | relationships integrity | | raman-fitting | 1/3 | numeric peak values (G/2D) | | cron-broken-network | 1/2 | curl output CONTENT (file existed) | | vim-terminal-task | 4/5 | executable bit | | configure-git-webserver | 0/1 | left repo in post-test state | | build-linux-kernel-qemu | test crashed | verified with own initramfs, never the provided one | | hf-model-inference | 2/4 | model download incomplete (token discovery?) | | create-bucket | 0/2 | credentials declared missing after a shallow hunt | This is not a capability ceiling — it is a **verification-discipline gap**: the agent plans correctly, executes almost correctly, and never re-checks the produced STATE against the task TEXT before declaring done. ## Architecture Two named components, no new UI: - **FinalizeGate** (prompt contract, subject: the agent's own declaration of completion): in unattended/bench mode the system prompt appends a finalize contract — before ANY final summary, the agent (a) re-quotes every explicit requirement from the task text as a checklist, (b) verifies each item with a real command against the produced state (not memory), (c) fixes or explicitly reports every unmet item. Invariant: a final answer whose checklist is not all-verified is a protocol violation the harness can detect (see TaskLedger). - **TaskLedger** (session record, subject: the checklist itself): the checklist + per-item verification command/result persist as a hidden session record type (like `model_request_summary`), so (a) post-mortems can see WHAT was self-checked (this autopsy would have taken minutes, not hours), (b) the bench summary can report near-miss proximity ("failed 1 of 7 checks, checklist verified 6"), (c) CI can REG-gate the contract's presence in unattended runs. ```mermaid flowchart LR T[task text] --> CL[checklist extraction
agent-authored] CL --> V{verify each item
REAL command vs state} V -->|fail| FIX[fix + re-verify] V -->|pass| L[TaskLedger record
item, cmd, result] L --> FIN[final answer allowed] ``` ## Capability surface (what "verify before declaring" means — exhaustively) | capability | subject | shape | |---|---|---| | checklist extraction | the TASK TEXT (explicit requirements only: files, states, formats, permissions, endpoints) | agent-authored, quoted verbatim, one item per requirement | | state verification | the PRODUCED ENVIRONMENT (files, services, git state, processes) | real command per item; expected-vs-actual noted; no "I wrote it earlier" | | permission/executable checks | created scripts/binaries | `test -x`, shebang present — the vim lesson as a named item | | final-state discipline | the REPO/SERVICE the task describes | after any destructive self-test, restore the state the task's canonical flow ends in |

**Bug**: Release-pipeline CI run 39432336443 (tag v1.0.611) went red — `Core tests (shard 3/4)` and (downstream, mechanically) `Quality gate` — although every shard-3 test passed.

**Root cause**: The `test-core` shard jobs upload their evidence artifacts (`coverage-shard-N`, `junit-shard-N`) as bare `actions/upload-artifact@v7.0.2` steps with **no gh-1412 one-shot retry** (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `test-core` job, steps after `Format coverage to lcov`). In run 39432336443 the `junit-shard-3` upload died on a single transient GitHub blob-storage error — `Failed to FinalizeArtifact: Received non-retryable error: Failed request: (404) Not Found: artifact not found` — after the bytes had already uploaded. The step failure red'd the shard job (the `dart test --coverage (shard 3)` step itself is green), the `Quality gate` job then read `test-core = failure` and failed with `Quality gate FAILED: a leg is failure (test-core)`. The identical failure class is already documented in-repo: gh-1412 (validation run 37807820733, `Failed to FinalizeArtifact: ECONNRESET`, 68/68 tests green) added the bounded retry to the `pty-integration-linux` evidence uploads only; `test-core` never got the same protection.

**Impact**: Any transient artifact-service hiccup during a sharded unit-test upload reds a `v*` tag run of the release pipeline (`ci.yml` fires on `v*` tags), files a `[ci-red]` issue and blocks the release flow — with the test verdict itself perfectly green. Non-deterministic, not tied to any code change.

**Evidence**:
- Failed step log (job 118669949363): `##[error]Failed to FinalizeArtifact: Received non-retryable error: Failed request: (404) Not Found: artifact not found`; the run's artifact list contains `junit-shard-0/1/2` but no `junit-shard-3` (half-registered, finalize lost).
- The sibling `release`-event run of the same tag (39432339703) is fully green, including `junit-shard-3` — confirms transient infra, not product code.
- Repo precedent comment: ci.yml "gh-1412: each evidence upload carries a one-shot retry … transient `Failed to FinalizeArtifact: ECONNRESET` from GitHub's blob storage" + guard `test/ci_pty_artifact_upload_retry_guard_test.dart` (pty leg only).

**Fix approach**: Extend the established gh-1412 pattern to the `test-core` shard uploads: give `coverage-shard-N` and `junit-shard-N` primaries step `id`s and follow each with a same-pin retry step (`overwrite: true`, gated on `always() && steps.<id>.outcome == 'failure'`, same artifact name/path/retention).       # maps test FILES to shards (file-level units — test/cli alone was

## Quality gates (pre-commit hook: `scripts/pre-commit`)

The single CI gate is the SM pre-merge validation run (gh-1537): the
machine SM (#687, `machine-sm.yml` → factory-sm) updates the branch onto
main, dispatches `ci.yml` on the updated head, and merges only when green
— the tree that lands is byte-identical to the validated tree, so the
retired post-merge main CI run was pure repetition (and #1522's
tag-sourced versions remove the release-bot commits that retriggered it —
fewer main pushes → less SM queue churn). `ci.yml` fires on `v*` tags
(release pipeline), the 2h auto-release coalesce schedule, `release:
published`, and workflow_dispatch ONLY — never on `push: [main]`. The
serialized-validation invariant is alarmed by `sm-merge-guard.yml`: every
main push must carry a tree covered by a successful dispatched
validation, else one deduplicated `sm-guard` issue files (no nightly
backstop, per the owner's directive).

Issue #177 restructured CI so a PR pays only for what it touched. The hook
is a thin wrapper over `scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh`; CI is NOT the same
process — it implements the same stages as parallel jobs, and since
issue #194 its PR path classification runs through the SAME script
(`ci_fast_gate.sh --dry-run` in the `changes` job). One classifier, one
set of thresholds; parity is checkable by diffing the hook's
`GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP` markers against the stages the CI changes job
logs for the same diff. Path filters: docs/markdown/prompts-only →
size+analyze; lib/bin/test/example/pubspec → +tests, coverage, CRAP,
jscpd + cross-module dupx; `test/integration/**` → + `integration-mock`
(issue #551: the no-key legs run per-PR); flutter_app/packages → +dupx,
flutter analyze+tests;
scripts/.github/crap4dart.yaml/unknown → everything (safe default, E2 —
holds in CI too). Hook-only extras: dart format self-heal of staged files
and `scripts/check_goldens.py --quick` (skipped for docs-only commits).

- `dart analyze` + dart format clean (explicit dirs — `yoclip/` is a
  standalone video workspace with its own toolchain); example app also
  `flutter analyze --no-fatal-infos --no-fatal-warnings`.
- `dart test` green (integration-tagged excluded from test-core — issue
  #551: `test/integration/**` changes also run the `integration-mock` leg
  per-PR: no-key legs via `MockLlmServer`, `--exclude-tags llm,browser-ext,
  perf,pty`; child-agent-spawn PTY tests carry `pty` and stay in nightly
  (issue #553). Tag-only CI = llm smoke + publish + binaries; nightly keeps
  the full real-provider suite (pty-integration). Since gh-1537 there are
  NO main CI runs — "tag-only" is literal: tags/dispatch/schedule only.
  **The Quality gate is deterministic-only (gh-1199): mock LLM everywhere,
  live models never.** Real-provider files carry
  `@Tags(['integration', 'llm'])` and run ONLY in the tag-only
  provider-smoke job and nightly with secrets — the per-PR integration
  shards exclude them at selection (`shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm`) AND
  at invocation (`--exclude-tags browser-ext,llm`), so a model's mood can
  never block a merge. The boundary is self-enforcing:
  `scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py` (static-gate step + pinned audit)
  fails any integration-tagged file that looks live without the `llm` tag;
  `test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart` proves the shard
  selection stays live-free. Real-model verification belongs to the bench
  harnesses (terminal-bench / harbor / MLS-Bench) run under supervision,
  plus manual `dart test --tags "integration && llm"` for debugging — NO
  scheduled-or-gate live runs in the PR path. A proven flake (red in ≥2

[GOAL] Near-miss elimination: FinalizeGate contract + TaskLedger — the agent verifies produced state against task text before declaring done --- ## Goal — Near-miss elimination: the agent finishes, then verifies (v1) One sentence: **an unattended fa agent stops declaring success on intent and starts declaring it on re-verified state — the single-check near-miss class dies.** ### The data that frames this card (run 37736364517, final 43/80 = 54%) Of 37 failures, 16 are honest stalls (race-class, #1406), ~5 harness/task-induced (#1407/#1408), and **~13 are near-misses: the agent passes 4–6 of the task's 5–7 checks and loses on exactly ONE detail** — verified from parser verdicts: | task | passed / total | the one miss | |---|---|---| | pytorch-model-cli | 5/6 | final CLI output (chmod +x WAS done — the vim lesson generalized!) | | nginx-request-logging | 6/7 | index page content | | reshard-c4-data | 1/2 | the revert step | | organization-json-generator | 3/4 | relationships integrity | | raman-fitting | 1/3 | numeric peak values (G/2D) | | cron-broken-network | 1/2 | curl output CONTENT (file existed) | | vim-terminal-task | 4/5 | executable bit | | configure-git-webserver | 0/1 | left repo in post-test state | | build-linux-kernel-qemu | test crashed | verified with own initramfs, never the provided one | | hf-model-inference | 2/4 | model download incomplete (token discovery?) | | create-bucket | 0/2 | credentials declared missing after a shallow hunt | This is not a capability ceiling — it is a **verification-discipline gap**: the agent plans correctly, executes almost correctly, and never re-checks the produced STATE against the task TEXT before declaring done. ## Architecture Two named components, no new UI: - **FinalizeGate** (prompt contract, subject: the agent's own declaration of completion): in unattended/bench mode the system prompt appends a finalize contract — before ANY final summary, the agent (a) re-quotes every explicit requirement from the task text as a checklist, (b) verifies each item with a real command against the produced state (not memory), (c) fixes or explicitly reports every unmet item. Invariant: a final answer whose checklist is not all-verified is a protocol violation the harness can detect (see TaskLedger). - **TaskLedger** (session record, subject: the checklist itself): the checklist + per-item verification command/result persist as a hidden session record type (like `model_request_summary`), so (a) post-mortems can see WHAT was self-checked (this autopsy would have taken minutes, not hours), (b) the bench summary can report near-miss proximity ("failed 1 of 7 checks, checklist verified 6"), (c) CI can REG-gate the contract's presence in unattended runs. ```mermaid flowchart LR T[task text] --> CL[checklist extraction
agent-authored] CL --> V{verify each item
REAL command vs state} V -->|fail| FIX[fix + re-verify] V -->|pass| L[TaskLedger record
item, cmd, result] L --> FIN[final answer allowed] ``` ## Capability surface (what "verify before declaring" means — exhaustively) | capability | subject | shape | |---|---|---| | checklist extraction | the TASK TEXT (explicit requirements only: files, states, formats, permissions, endpoints) | agent-authored, quoted verbatim, one item per requirement | | state verification | the PRODUCED ENVIRONMENT (files, services, git state, processes) | real command per item; expected-vs-actual noted; no "I wrote it earlier" | | permission/executable checks | created scripts/binaries | `test -x`, shebang present — the vim lesson as a named item | | final-state discipline | the REPO/SERVICE the task describes | after any destructive self-test, restore the state the task's canonical flow ends in |

{"path":"outputs/rca.md","content":"# Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: Release-pipeline CI run 39432336443 (tag v1.0.611) went red — `Core tests (shard 3/4)` and (downstream, mechanically) `Quality gate` — although every shard-3 test passed.

**Root cause**: The `test-core` shard jobs upload their evidence artifacts (`coverage-shard-N`, `junit-shard-N`) as bare `actions/upload-artifact@v7.0.2` steps with **no gh-1412 one-shot retry** (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `test-core` job, steps after `Format coverage to lcov`). In run 39432336443 the `junit-shard-3` upload died on a single transient GitHub blob-storage error — `Failed to FinalizeArtifact: Received non-retryable error: Failed request: (404) Not Found: artifact not found` — after the bytes had already uploaded. The step failure red'd the shard job (the `dart test --coverage (shard 3)` step itself is green), the `Quality gate` job then read `test-core = failure` and failed with `Quality gate FAILED: a leg is failure (test-core)`. The identical failure class is already documented in-repo: gh-1412 (validation run 37807820733, `Failed to FinalizeArtifact: ECONNRESET`, 68/68 tests green) added the bounded retry to the `pty-integration-linux` evidence uploads only; `test-core` never got the same protection.

**Impact**: Any transient artifact-service hiccup during a sharded unit-test upload reds a `v*` tag run of the release pipeline (`ci.yml` fires on `v*` tags), files a `[ci-red]` issue and blocks the release flow — with the test verdict itself perfectly green. Non-deterministic, not tied to any code change.

**Evidence**:
- Failed step log (job 118669949363): `##[error]Failed to FinalizeArtifact: Received non-retryable error: Failed request: (404) Not Found: artifact not found`; the run's artifact list contains `junit-shard-0/1/2` but no `junit-shard-3` (half-registered, finalize lost).
- The sibling `release`-event run of the same tag (39432339703) is fully green, including `junit-shard-3` — confirms transient infra, not product code.
- Repo precedent comment: ci.yml "gh-1412: each evidence upload carries a one-shot retry … transient `Failed to FinalizeArtifact: ECONNRESET` from GitHub's blob storage" + guard `test/ci_pty_artifact_upload_retry_guard_test.dart` (pty leg only).

**Fix approach**: Extend the established gh-1412 pattern to the `test-core` shard uploads: give `coverage-shard-N` and `junit-shard-N` primaries step `id`s and follow each with a same-pin retry step (`overwrite: true`, gated on `always() && steps.<id>.outcome == 'failure'`, same artifact name/path/retention). A transient finalize failure gets exactly one more attempt; a genuinely dead endpoint still fails the shard loudly. Guarded by a new YAML-level static test mirroring the pty guard (`test/ci_core_shard_upload_retry_guard_test.dart`).

**Previous attempt**: N/A — first development pass on this ticket.

      # maps test FILES to shards (file-level units — test/cli alone was
      # half the suite's runtime and undivisible as a dir-unit); rebalanced
      # weekly by shard-rebalance.yml from junit durations. Bootstrap here
      # is filecount-balanced; the first weekly junit rebalance converges

      # lib/src/cli hits from them), so the sharded unit run above skips

      # (>= 80% ratchet, PR diff-coverage, CRAP — jsr_cli.dart at 0% reads
      # CRAP 156 > 12), so they run into shard 0's coverage dir; the gate
      # merge is a union, so one shard carrying them is enough. Keep this
      # list in sync with scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh stage_test_core (gh-1538
      # retired the nightly full-quality copy — the pre-merge gate is the

## Quality gates (pre-commit hook: `scripts/pre-commit`)

The single CI gate is the SM pre-merge validation run (gh-1537): the
machine SM (#687, `machine-sm.yml` → factory-sm) updates the branch onto
main, dispatches `ci.yml` on the updated head, and merges only when green
— the tree that lands is byte-identical to the validated tree, so the
retired post-merge main CI run was pure repetition (and #1522's
tag-sourced versions remove the release-bot commits that retriggered it —
fewer main pushes → less SM queue churn). `ci.yml` fires on `v*` tags
(release pipeline), the 2h auto-release coalesce schedule, `release:
published`, and workflow_dispatch ONLY — never on `push: [main]`. The
serialized-validation invariant is alarmed by `sm-merge-guard.yml`: every
main push must carry a tree covered by a successful dispatched
validation, else one deduplicated `sm-guard` issue files (no nightly
backstop, per the owner's directive).

Issue #177 restructured CI so a PR pays only for what it touched. The hook
is a thin wrapper over `scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh`; CI is NOT the same
process — it implements the same stages as parallel jobs, and since
issue #194 its PR path classification runs through the SAME script
(`ci_fast_gate.sh --dry-run` in the `changes` job). One classifier, one
set of thresholds; parity is checkable by diffing the hook's
`GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP` markers against the stages the CI changes job
logs for the same diff. Path filters: docs/markdown/prompts-only →
size+analyze; lib/bin/test/example/pubspec → +tests, coverage, CRAP,
jscpd + cross-module dupx; `test/integration/**` → + `integration-mock`
(issue #551: the no-key legs run per-PR); flutter_app/packages → +dupx,
flutter analyze+tests;
scripts/.github/crap4dart.yaml/unknown → everything (safe default, E2 —
holds in CI too). Hook-only extras: dart format self-heal of staged files
and `scripts/check_goldens.py --quick` (skipped for docs-only commits).

- `dart analyze` + dart format clean (explicit dirs — `yoclip/` is a
  standalone video workspace with its own toolchain); example app also
  `flutter analyze --no-fatal-infos --no-fatal-warnings`.
- `dart test` green (integration-tagged excluded from test-core — issue
  #551: `test/integration/**` changes also run the `integration-mock` leg
  per-PR: no-key legs via `MockLlmServer`, `--exclude-tags llm,browser-ext,
  perf,pty`; child-agent-spawn PTY tests carry `pty` and stay in nightly
  (issue #553). Tag-only CI = llm smoke + publish + binaries; nightly keeps
  the full real-provider suite (pty-integration). Since gh-1537 there are
  NO main CI runs — "tag-only" is literal: tags/dispatch/schedule only.
  **The Quality gate is deterministic-only (gh-1199): mock LLM everywhere,
  live models never.** Real-provider files carry
  `@Tags(['integration', 'llm'])` and run ONLY in the tag-only
  provider-smoke job and nightly with secrets — the per-PR integration
  shards exclude them at selection (`shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm`) AND
  at invocation (`--exclude-tags browser-ext,llm`), so a model's mood can
  never block a merge. The boundary is self-enforcing:
  `scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py` (static-gate step + pinned audit)
